content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I've created custom graphics in [product_name] and loaded them onto an SD card I had available (a new 32GB microSDHC card). Everything seems to work well, but I'm curious about how durable this SD card is. If I'm just using a regular SD card, could it wear out quickly? Is there anything I can do to extend its lifespan? Thanks in advance!
Why do you think the SD card would wear out?

Now I understand. I thought that displaying analog values with [product_name] would result in continuous data writing to the SD card. I realize that's not the case—it would not be practical if updates to values like temperature caused the card to wear out quickly. Thanks for clarifying.
[product_name] does not store process values on the SD card.

analysis.insight_summary: Discussion centers on concerns about SD card endurance when used with [product_name] graphics, especially regarding frequent data updates and their effect on card wear. There is some misunderstanding about whether real-time values are often written to the card, indicating the need for clearer documentation about how the product interacts with SD cards.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the SD card to remain reliable during ongoing use and is looking for assurance that frequent data updates will not reduce its lifespan prematurely. The user seeks clarification on how the product manages data writing to SD cards.
